content.text: If you purchase a product or register for an account through one of the links on our site, we may receive compensation. Learn more > With the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, the Dallas Wings selected another UConn star.One year after Dallas landed a franchise cornerstone in Paige Bueckers, the team acquired Huskies shooting guard Azzi Fudd, who won the 2025 national championship with Bueckers."I'm excited to play again with Paige," Fudd told ESPN's Holly Rowe. "She's an incredible person, an incredible player, and it's gonna be a lot of fun." Olivia Miles (Minnesota Lynx), Awa Fam Thiam (Seattle Storm), Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics) and Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) rounded out the top five.After winning the 2026 national title, UCLA broke the record for most players selected from a single school in the first round with Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo), Angela Dugalic (Washington Mystics) and Gianna Kneepkens (Connecticut Sun) joining Betts and Jaquez on the draft board.Check out the full list of picks from the 2026 WNBA Draft below.WNBA Draft picks 2026: Full list of results from Rounds 1-3First roundPickTeamPlayer1.Dallas WingsAzzi Fudd, UConn2.Minnesota Lynx (via Sky)Olivia Miles, TCU3.Seattle Storm (via Sparks)Awa Fam Thiam, Spain4.Washington MysticsLauren Betts, UCLA5.Chicago Sky (via Sun)Gabriela Jaquez, UCLA6.Toronto TempoKiki Rice, UCLA7.Portland FireIyana Martin Carrion, Spain8.Golden State ValkyriesFlau'jae Johnson, LSU*9.Washington Mystics (via Storm)Angela Dugalic, UCLA10.Indiana FeverRaven Johnson, South Carolina11.Washington Mystics (via Liberty)Cotie McMahon, Ole Miss12.Connecticut Sun (via Mercury)Nell Angloma, France13.Atlanta DreamMadina Okot, South Carolina14.Seattle Storm (via Aces)Taina Mair, Duke15.Connecticut Sun (via Lynx)Gianna Kneepkens, UCLA*Traded to Seattle StormSecond roundPickTeamPlayer16.Seattle Storm (via Wings)Marta Suarez, TCU*17.Portland Fire (via Sky)Frieda Buhner, Germany18.Connecticut SunCharlisse Leger-Walker, UCLA19.Washington MysticsCassandre Prosper, Notre Dame20.Los Angeles SparksTa'Niya Latson, South Carolina21.Chicago Sky (via Fire)Latasha Lattimore, Ole Miss22.Toronto TempoTeonni Key, Kentucky23.Golden State ValkyriesAshlon Jackson, Duke24.Los Angeles Sparks (via Storm)Chance Gray, Ohio State25.Indiana FeverJustine Pissott, Vanderbilt26.Toronto Tempo (via Liberty)Saffron Shiels, Australia27.Phoenix MercuryInes Pitarch-Granel, France28.Atlanta DreamIndya Nivar, North Carolina29.
